newsitem.title: INDIA: India foreign currency assets close to $18 bln - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India foreign currency assets close to $18 bln - RBI.

text.p: India's foreign currency assets were close to $18 billion at the end of August 1996, the deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Friday.

"The foreign currency assets of the Reserve Bank which were a little over $17 billion at the end of March 1996 were a little less than $18 billion at the end of August 1996," S.S. Tarapore told a meeting of businessmen.

He said the latest figure was after taking into account a payment of $750 million out of the reserves under the foreign currency non-resident account (FCNRA) deposit accounts held by expatriate Indians and over $450 million spent on repurchases and interest payments to the International Monetary Fund.
"The outstanding forward exchange liabilities of the RBI have been halved from $2.2 billion at the end of March 1996 to $1.1 billion at the end of August 1996," Tarapore said.

He said net inflows from foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in 1996/97 (April-March) up to early August 1996 have been a little less than $1.5 billion and direct investments and GDRs were running at a level well above the comparable period of the previous year.
"The inflation rate has held remarkably well around 5.0-5.5 percent and developments in the real sector point to the absence of any commodity shortages," he said.
Tarapore admitted that 1996/97 would be a "problematic year" for India because of large external repayments. "But we seem to be coming out of it," he said.
